entities.summary:
Louis de Bourbon-Vendôme, born on 11 January 1493 in the Château de Ham, was a French prince du sang and religious leader. He was the son of Francis, Count of Vendôme and Marie of Luxembourg.

As a member of the powerful House of Bourbon, Louis de Bourbon-Vendôme played a significant role in the religious landscape of Western Europe during the 16th century. He was a key figure in the Counter-Reformation, a movement aimed at countering the spread of Protestantism. Louis de Bourbon-Vendôme was also a patron of the arts and architecture, and his influence can be seen in the design of several churches and monasteries in France.

Despite his significant contributions to the religious and artistic communities, Louis de Bourbon-Vendôme's legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his more famous relatives, such as Henry IV of France. However, his impact on the development of religious thought and practice in 16th-century France cannot be overstated.

One of Louis de Bourbon-Vendôme's most lasting legacies is the establishment of the Bourbon dynasty, which would go on to shape the course of European history for centuries to come.
